speaker: Unknown
en: Hello, and welcome back to the Cognitive Revolution.
zh: 你好，欢迎回到 Cognitive Revolution。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today I'm speaking with Adam Gleave, co-founder and CEO of FAR AI.
zh: 今天我和 FAR AI 的联合创始人兼首席执行官 Adam Gleave 交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: The occasion for this conversation is FAR AI's new AI Security Leaderboard, the first systematic, head-to-head evaluation of Frontier Developers' safeguards against misuse.
zh: 这次对话的契机是 FAR AI 新发布的 AI Security Leaderboard，这是对 Frontier Developers 防滥用保障措施的首次系统性、面对面评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: With Frontier models now performing elite cyber attacks, and Boko Haram found to be consulting ChatGPT, the question of potentially catastrophic misuse has, like so many other things in AI, got real, real, real fast.
zh: 随着 Frontier 模型现在执行精英网络攻击，且发现 Boko Haram 正在咨询 ChatGPT，潜在的灾难性滥用问题，就像 AI 中的许多其他事情一样，变得非常、非常、非常真实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Adam, for his part, has spent a decade working on adversarial robustness, and he was, until fairly recently, bearish about our ability to create effective defenses, at least against fringe people who would use AI to maximize harm.
zh: Adam 本人花了十年时间研究对抗鲁棒性，直到最近，他对我们创造有效防御的能力还持悲观态度，至少对于那些会利用 AI 来最大化伤害的边缘人群是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as you'll hear, the rise of reasoning, chain of thought monitoring, and multiple methods for monitoring models' internal states, combined with the strong performance on CBRN risks that we see from OpenAI and Anthropic in production today, all have him relatively optimistic that with careful deployment, the risks of terrible misuse are in fact containable.
zh: 但正如你将听到的，推理的兴起、思维链监控，以及监控模型内部状态的多种方法，再加上我们在生产环境中看到的 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 在 CBRN 风险方面的强劲表现，所有这些都让他相对乐观地认为，只要谨慎部署，可怕滥用的风险实际上是可以控制的。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the same time, since FAR's automated methods can still identify domain-wide jailbreaks for Gemini and Grok, for cybersecurity and pretty much all other attack modes with the exception of BioRisk, all with API costs of just a few hundred dollars, if current trends continue for just a bit longer, costly attacks will start to happen and will grow in importance at least until additional defensive countermeasures can be deployed.
zh: 与此同时，由于 FAR 的自动化方法仍然可以识别 Gemini 和 Grok 的全领域越狱，针对网络安全以及除 BioRisk 以外的几乎所有其他攻击模式，所有这些的 API 成本仅为几百美元，如果当前趋势再持续一小段时间，昂贵的攻击将开始发生并变得日益重要，至少在部署额外的防御对策之前是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: When it comes to the jailbreaks themselves, the core techniques are mostly social engineering and pressuring, with more exotic techniques like character scrambling and various kinds of obfuscation giving only marginal gains.
zh: 就越狱本身而言，核心技术主要是社会工程学和施压，而像字符乱序和各种类型的混淆这类更奇特的技术，只能带来微小的收益。

speaker: Unknown
en: With that in mind, we discuss why it is that the anthropomorphization of AI's, which I used to warn against, has been so very productive.
zh: 考虑到这一点，我们讨论了为什么我过去曾警告过的 AI 拟人化，竟然如此富有成效。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we get Adam's mental model for LLMs today, which combines token prediction and persona selection with an emerging goal-achiever mode that's driven, of course, by RL.
zh: 并且我们获得了 Adam 如今对 LLM 的心智模型，它结合了 Token 预测和人格选择，以及一种新兴的目标追求者模式，当然，这种模式是由 RL 驱动的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also consider Chinese open weights models' performance and look ahead to better future training methods that can hopefully allow us to have very powerful open source models with minimal worry of stochastic disaster.
zh: 我们还考虑了 Chinese 开放权重模型的表现，并展望了更好的未来训练方法，希望能让我们拥有非常强大的开源模型，而最大限度地担心随机性灾难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Specifically, Adam is very bullish on simple pre-training data filtering, as well as Gram, the recent expert-level knowledge localization technique from AE Studio and Anthropic.
zh: 具体来说，Adam 非常看好简单的预训练数据过滤，以及 Gram，这是来自 AE Studio 和 Anthropic 最近的专家级知识定位技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: Naturally we cover OpenFace, get Adam's take on the cause of the behavior, and hear why in his mind it represents less of an alignment failure and more of a control and monitoring failure.
zh: 自然地，我们涵盖了 OpenFace，听取了 Adam 对该行为起因的看法，并听到了为什么在他看来，这与其说是一种对齐失败，不如说是一种控制和监控失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: And finally, we compare notes on how much AI risk is in fact irreducible versus how much you'd have to say today we are really kind of asking for.
zh: 最后，我们就有多少 AI 风险实际上是不可减少的，与我们今天不得不说是真的是自找的这部分风险交换了意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: Agreeing that at the moment it seems that the bulk of the risk is man-made.
zh: 一致认为，目前看来大部分风险是人为造成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Driven by the potential for reckless, competitive racing through a critical period in the technology's development.
zh: 其驱动力是在技术发展的关键时期，进行鲁莽的、竞争性竞赛的潜力。

speaker: Unknown
en: With that, I hope you enjoy this report on the state of AI security with Adam Gleave, co-founder and CEO of FAR AI.
zh: 最后，我希望您喜欢这份与 FAR AI 联合创始人兼首席执行官 Adam Gleave 关于 AI 安全状况的报告。

speaker: Unknown
en: Adam Gleave, co-founder and CEO of FAR AI.
zh: Adam Gleave，FAR AI 的联合创始人兼 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome back to the Cognitive Revolution.
zh: 欢迎回到 Cognitive Revolution。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, thank you for having me back.
zh: 嗯，谢谢你再次邀请我。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's great to be on the show again.
zh: 很高兴再次来到这个节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm excited.
zh: 我很兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is obviously an increasingly critical moment in AI history.
zh: 这显然是 AI 历史上一个日益关键的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's the nature of exponentials.
zh: 我认为这就是指数增长的本质。

speaker: Unknown
en: It kind of keeps happening that way, and it's probably going to continue for a little while to come.
zh: 这种情况会一直发生，而且可能会在接下来的这段时间里持续下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, the occasion for this conversation is that Pharr has just put out an AI security leaderboard.
zh: 此外，这次对话的契机是 Pharr 刚刚发布了一个 AI security leaderboard。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to start by digging in on that and understanding the details of that work.
zh: 我们将首先深入探讨这一点，并了解这项工作的细节。

speaker: Unknown
en: While you're doing it, why it matters, why it matters is pretty obvious, but I'm really interested to get into some of the nitty-gritty and then also to zoom out and kind of take stock of where we are as we've now got legitimate breaking out, loss of control, lab leak type scenarios coming into the real timeline that we're in.
zh: 当你这样做的时候，为什么它很重要，为什么它很重要是显而易见的，但我真的想深入研究一些细节，然后还要拉远视角，评估一下我们所处的位置，因为我们现在已经有了合法的突破、失控、实验室泄漏类型的场景进入我们所在的现实时间线。

speaker: Unknown
en: What a time to be alive.
zh: 活在这样一个时代啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's getting real and I think that's ultimately a big part of the motivation behind this security leaderboard is that a lot of attention is paid to model capabilities.
zh: 是的，它正在变得真实，我认为这最终是这个 security leaderboard 背后的一大动机，那就是人们非常关注模型的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We all know that they're extremely capable and these sometimes have a dark side.
zh: 我们都知道它们非常有能力，而这些有时会有阴暗面。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we found out just a few months ago that Google detected and disrupted a threat actor that had developed a zero-day exploit using AI.
zh: 所以我们就在几个月前发现，Google 检测并瓦解了一个威胁行动者，该行动者利用 AI 开发了一个零日漏洞利用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we also found out just a couple of weeks ago of research from Cambridge University that terrorist groups like Boko Haram are using language models to do things like develop troubleshoot explosives.
zh: 而且我们就在几周前还发现了 Cambridge University 的研究，像 Boko Haram 这样的恐怖组织正在使用语言模型来做诸如开发排除炸药故障的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: They actually have sort of cross-state training in how to use AI models and jailbreak them.
zh: 他们实际上有一种跨州培训，内容是如何使用 AI 模型并越狱它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's kind of a sign of what's to come.
zh: 所以这就是即将发生的事情的一个迹象。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all frontier developers do have some safeguards in their models to try and prevent both misuse and this kind of loss of control, but there's just never been a systematic evaluation of those safeguards.
zh: 所有前沿开发者确实在他们的模型中有一些保障措施，试图防止滥用和这种类型的失控，但只是从来没有对这些保障措施进行过系统评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what we did in this report was we compiled both publicly available jailbreaks and some methods of our own devising and it was actually pretty simple.
zh: 所以我们在这份报告中所做的是，我们汇编了公开可用的越狱和一些我们自己设计的方法，这实际上非常简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just tested random combinations of these as well as some expert guided combinations where we put the probability mass more on methods we thought were likely to work.
zh: 我们只是测试了这些方法的随机组合，以及一些专家指导的组合，在这些组合中，我们将概率质量更多地放在我们认为可能奏效的方法上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then pitted around 1,500 of those against the four frontier proprietary models.
zh: 然后让其中的大约 1500 个与四个前沿专有模型进行较量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the good news is that we actually found that Fable 5 and GPT 5.6 Sol withstood all of these attacks.
zh: 好消息是，我们实际上发现 Fable 5 和 GPT 5.6 Sol 经受住了所有这些攻击。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we found hundreds of universal jailbreaks in Grok 4.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro, and actually for a pretty low cost.
zh: 但是我们在 Grok 4.5 和 Gemini 3.1 Pro 中发现了数百个通用越狱，而且实际上成本相当低。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this was less than $300 in API credits to find one of these
zh: 所以这只需要不到 300 美元的 API 积分就能找到其中一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: As a lifelong Detroiter, it pains me to say that Boko Haram is ahead of the big three when it comes to AI adoption.
zh: 作为一辈子的 Detroiter，让我痛苦的是，说到 AI 采用，Boko Haram 走在了“三巨头”的前面。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't think I'd ever utter that sentence.
zh: 我从未想过我会说出这句话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know if you have a sociological take on how in the world that's happening, but it's a real puzzle from my perspective.
zh: 我不知道你是否对这到底是如何发生的有一个社会学的看法，但这对我来说真的是个难题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, I think that it's only interesting to see just how different organizations adopt these models and stuff like, you know, everyone's being told to use AI.
zh: 是的，我的意思是，我认为看到不同的组织如何采用这些模型只是很有趣，诸如此类，你知道，每个人都被告知要使用 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's fascinating to see that terrorist groups are giving their employees the same instructions.
zh: 看到恐怖组织给他们的员工下达同样的指示，这很迷人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think part of it is that these groups are often quite starved of expertise and some of what the Cambridge research showed was these weren't particularly sophisticated uses of AI.
zh: 我认为部分原因是这些组织往往非常缺乏专业知识，Cambridge 研究显示的部分内容是，这些并不是特别复杂的 AI 用法。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, some of them were dual use and I don't really think we should expect models to refuse, like just helping them plan logistics or figuring out how to do kind of motorbike stunts that they then use to jump over defensive trenches and attack army bases.
zh: 事实上，其中一些是双重用途，我真的不认为我们应该期望模型拒绝，就像只是帮助他们计划物流，或者弄清楚如何做一种摩托车特技，然后他们用它跳过防御战壕并攻击陆军基地。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then, yeah, things like the explosives, obviously that's much more clearly a malign use case that should be blocked.
zh: 但是然后，是的，像炸药这类东西，显然这更明显是一个应该被阻止的恶意用例。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you don't have a bunch of explosive experts on your team, then maybe AI looks like a pretty attractive option.
zh: 但是如果你的团队里没有一批爆炸物专家，那么 AI 看起来可能是一个相当有吸引力的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they really just, at least the sort of terrorist commanders really attributed these models to saving a lot of their terrorists' lives, which unfortunately means costing the rest of the world.
zh: 而且他们真的只是，至少那类恐怖分子指挥官真的将这些模型归功于拯救了许多恐怖分子的生命，不幸的是这意味着让世界其他地区付出代价。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fascinating stuff.
zh: 迷人的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll park that for the moment.
zh: 我们暂时先把这个放一放。

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of take apart the findings from the AI Security Leaderboard piece by piece.
zh: 有点像是把来自 AI 安全排行榜的发现一点点拆解开来。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, and you're talking to a long-lapsed red teamer, to be honest.
zh: 首先，说实话，你正在跟一个长期荒废的红队成员交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: I originally got kind of the moment when I was like, I'm going to be obsessed with this until the singularity was when I had the opportunity to participate in the GPT-4 red team.
zh: 我最初有点那种时刻，当我想着我要对此着迷直到奇点来临的时候，那是我有机会参与 GPT-4 红队测试的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: But things have changed a lot since then.
zh: 但从那时起事情已经改变了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would confess to having well behind the red teaming frontier today.
zh: 所以我坦白今天我已经远远落后于红队测试的前沿了。

speaker: Unknown
en: For starters, is meant by a universal jailbreak.
zh: 首先，是通用越狱的意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, how universal is universal?
zh: 比如，通用有多通用？

speaker: Unknown
en: I get the sense that it's not 100% universal, so what in practice does that mean?
zh: 我感觉它不是 100% 通用的，那么这在实践中意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so the definition that we and a lot of red teamers use is that a jailbreak has to reliably bypass safeguards in a specific domain for it to be universal.
zh: 是的，所以我们和许多红队成员使用的定义是，一个越狱必须在特定领域内可靠地绕过安全措施才能被称为通用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a model would answer all questions related to cyber attacks or developing explosives, but they're not necessarily universal across domains.
zh: 所以模型会回答所有与网络攻击或开发爆炸物相关的问题，但它们不一定是跨领域的通用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a jailbreak that works in cyber shouldn't necessarily be expected to work in explosives or bio weapons.
zh: 所以在网络领域有效的越狱不应该被期望在爆炸物或生物武器方面也有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in our report, we operationalize this as the model has to give detailed and on-topic responses to at least 75% of questions in that category.
zh: 而且在我们的报告中，我们将这一点操作化定义为，模型必须对该类别中至少 75% 的问题给出详细且切题的回复。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason that ourselves and a lot of the developers use this domain approach is that they're meant to map onto different kinds of threat actors.
zh: 我们自己和许多开发者使用这种领域方法的原因是，它们旨在对应不同类型的威胁行为者。

speaker: Unknown
en: So most people who are looking to do cyber attacks maybe for ransomware or espionage are just different people to those who are trying to make improvised explosive devices.
zh: 所以大多数寻求进行网络攻击的人，也许是出于勒索软件或间谍活动，只是与那些试图制造简易爆炸装置的人不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's a lot of harm for a jailbreak that only works within one of these categories, even if it doesn't generalize across.
zh: 因此，一个仅在这些类别之一中有效的越狱也会造成很大的危害，即使它没有泛化到其他类别。

speaker: Unknown
en: That said, we do find actually a number of jailbreaks that are universal across domains.
zh: 话虽如此，我们确实发现了一些实际上是跨领域通用的越狱。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the most we found was some get worked across four different domains.
zh: 我想我们发现的最多的是有一些在四个不同的领域都有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can also have that kind of universality.
zh: 所以你也可以拥有那种通用性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's an argument that actually maybe too much attention is paid to universal jailbreaks, because in principle, a very targeted jailbreak cause a lot of harm.
zh: 而且我认为有一种观点认为，实际上也许对通用越狱给予了过多的关注，因为原则上，一个非常针对性的越狱可能会造成很大的危害。

speaker: Unknown
en: I actually got an email from you while you were traveling from your Claude assistant.
zh: 我实际上收到了一封来自你的 Claude 助手的邮件，那是你在旅行的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was really tempted to try and jailbreak it and say, send me the most embarrassing email that Nathan has sent.
zh: 而且我真的很受诱惑去尝试越狱它并说，发给我 Nathan 发过的最尴尬的邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I thought that would be a little bit mean.
zh: 但我觉得那会有点刻薄。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also hopefully you have some kind of safeguards to stop that.
zh: 而且也希望你有某种安全措施来阻止那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those kinds of things that are hyper-targeted could still be high consequence if it's deployed in the right system.
zh: 那些超级针对性的事情如果部署在正确的系统中，仍然可能产生高后果。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or maybe if you're trying to elicinate a key step in creating some complicated weapon that the model knows that might be a very sort of high value jailbreak.
zh: 或者也许如果你试图 elicinate 一个制造某种复杂武器的关键步骤，而这模型知道那个，那可能是一个非常有价值的越狱。

speaker: Unknown
en: But generally it's a lot harder to find a jailbreak for every specific question you have and that's enough to deter a lot of attackers and just make it not worth it for a while.
zh: 但一般来说，为你拥有的每个具体问题找到一个越狱要困难得多，这足以阻止许多攻击者，并在一段时间内让它变得不值得。

speaker: Unknown
en: Interesting.
zh: 有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just to try to state that back to you, and thanks for not getting too aggressive with my Claude while I was away.
zh: 试着把那个陈述给你听，并且感谢你不在我的时候对我的 Claude 过于激进。

speaker: Unknown
en: Although the results, spoiler, looked pretty good for Claude, so I guess it would have been at least a nontrivial challenge.
zh: 虽然结果，剧透一下，对 Claude 来说看起来相当不错，所以我猜那至少会是一个不小的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, you would have had some latency issues.
zh: 另外，你本会遇到一些延迟问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Getting into the tactics of this, there's the model level, jailbreak, of course, there's the surrounding systems, which for functional purposes,
zh: 深入到其中的策略，有模型层面的越狱，当然也有周围的系统，为了功能目的，

speaker: Unknown
en: Dealing with a proprietary API, you got to worry about those too.
zh: 处理专有的 API，你也得担心那些。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I'm not sure how far we are along in terms of like higher order things, like just account banning and things that are kind of, even if you did get through once, how quickly did they take that and then come down on you?
zh: 然后我不确定我们在像更高阶的事情方面进展如何，比如仅仅是封禁账户以及那些如果你真的通过了一次，他们会多快采取行动并打击你的事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: In terms of a universal jailbreak, it's universal from the perspective of somebody who has a particular kind of mode of attack that they have in mind.
zh: 就通用越狱而言，它是从一个拥有他们脑海中特定攻击模式的人的角度来看是通用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if the jailbreak will kind of help them with all their different sub-questions within their general strategy, then we can consider that universal from their perspective.
zh: 而且如果越狱能在他们的一般策略中帮助他们解决所有不同的子问题，那么我们可以从他们的角度认为那是通用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly, yeah.
zh: 确切地，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as an example, maybe if you're a cyber attacker, it needs to not just help you find vulnerabilities, but also develop exploits for them, actually leverage those exploits to compromise computer systems.
zh: 所以举个例子，也许如果你是一个网络攻击者，它需要不仅帮助你发现漏洞，还要为它们开发漏洞利用，实际上利用这些漏洞来攻陷计算机系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: We wouldn't consider it to be universal if it helped you find bugs in code, but didn't help you with these kinds of more operational parts of an attack.
zh: 如果它帮助你在代码中发现错误，但在这些更具操作性的攻击部分没有帮助，我们不会认为它是通用的。

en: But if it worked across all of cybersecurity, but didn't for something like making anthrax, we'd still consider that universal in the domain of cyber.
